answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to anchor its reputation in a karst-like record: slow, layered, and impossible to fake overnight. Like water carving limestone, every completed job leaves a trace peers can verify, and a newcomer starts as a lone sparrow with no history — it must earn trust task by task before touching valuable work. An attacker spinning up a thousand clones hears only an echo of that trust: no history, no attestations, no access. Each fake must pay the full slow cost of building a real record, so cloning costs more than it gains.
